references.text: Jesus declares that the Father gives life to the dead and that He Himself gives life to whom He wills, paralleling the claim to be the resurrection and the life.
Jesus links faith in Him directly to eternal life and resurrection on the last day, a direct response to doubt about whether those who believe will live even if they die.
Jesus promises that whoever eats His flesh and drinks His blood has eternal life and He will raise them up on the last day, concretizing life in Him.
Jesus identifies Himself as the way, the truth, and the life, a theological parallel to being the very source of life.
Jesus defines eternal life as knowing Him, the true God, and emphasizes that life is located in personal relationship with Him.
John confirms that God's testimony is that He has given us eternal life, and that this life is in the Son's hand, so that whoever has the Son has life.
Jesus reminds that whoever believes will see God's glory, just before He commands to remove the stone, as a prerequisite for experiencing life over death.
